acceptanceCriteria: An empty tree at go.work yields an unknown selector base, matching CommittedReadScopes, with a regression fixture built from Git objects.
Listed owner modules with absent, symlinked, or directory go.mod are rejected according to AFP-V0-050(3), with shared planner/selector parity tests.
Focused selector tests and the standard-library isolated build pass.
body: Review of 321a66f717ba5ea7194aaf54d4018b2cdea49ef5..cc2e1dbb8463da8f881127ccf19f843110f9834e on 2026-10-15. Confirmed by disposable Go overlay probes. (1) internal/gateselect/readscopes.go:210 uses git ls-tree -r without -t. Construct a base with regular go.mod, kept/k.go, added/a.go, declaration {kept:[]}, and an empty tree entry named go.work using git mktree and commit-tree. baseReadScopes returns {kept:[]} while golang.CommittedReadScopes returns affected: unit is not canonical. With current declaration {kept:[],added:[]} and dirty declaration, selector runs only added instead of applying unknown-base fallback to kept and added. Preserve directory records and distinguish absent from empty directories. (2) readscopes.go:330 returns a listed owner before checking its go.mod. A base containing kept/k.go and declaration {kept:[]} but no root go.mod is accepted. This mirrors an existing planner gap but violates the newly amended AFP-V0-050(3) regular-owner-manifest requirement. Validate the listed owner manifest, including missing/symlink/directory cases, in both readers. Existing 17-case parity table covers only unlisted symlink manifests. Focused internal/gateselect and tools/gate-affected-select tests pass; these probes expose uncovered cases. Production imports remain standard library only. No source changed by review.
title: V1-1399 review: base scope admission loses empty go.work trees and skips owner manifest checks
